How to order coffee in Greece like a pro ☕🇬🇷 Recorded at @Pandrossos_Hotel_Paros 😍*invited  Greece’s coffee culture is on another level, with some iconic coffees that locals drink every single day. Of course, Greece also has cappuccinos, lattes, americanos, flat whites and all the other coffees you’re used to. But if you’re coming to Greece, you have to try ordering coffee the local way. Here’s exactly how it works. Step one: choose your coffee. ☕ Frappé Made with instant Nescafé and water, mixed until it becomes thick and foamy. The original Greek iced coffee. ☕ Freddo Espresso A cold espresso shaken with ice until it’s frothy and refreshing. ☕ Freddo Cappuccino A freddo espresso topped with a thick layer of cold milk foam. ☕ Ελληνικός Καφές (Ellinikós Kafés) Traditional Greek coffee made in a small briki pot. It’s served with the coffee grounds still inside the cup and is traditionally used for coffee reading. Now comes the important part. How sweet do you want it? 🖤 Σκέτο (Skéto) = no sugar 🤎 Μέτριο (Métrio) = medium sweet 🍯 Γλυκό (Glykó) = sweet You can also choose which sweetener you’d like: 🍬 Ζάχαρη (Záchari) = regular sugar 🤎 Μαύρη Ζάχαρη (Mávri Záchari) = brown sugar 💊 Ζαχαρίνη (Zacharíni) = saccharin 🌱 Στέβια (Stévia) = stevia If you want milk, you can ask for: 🥛 Γάλα (Gála) = regular milk 🌾 Γάλα Βρώμης (Gála Vrómis) = oat milk 🌰 Γάλα Αμυγδάλου (Gála Amygdálou) = almond milk 🥥 Γάλα Καρύδας (Gála Karýdas) = coconut milk 🌱 Γάλα Σόγιας (Gála Sógias) = soy milk If you’re ordering a freddo cappuccino, they’ll often ask if you want: ✨ Κανέλα (Kanéla) = cinnamon 🍫 Κακάο (Kakáo) = cacao And if you’re ordering a frappé, many places will also let you add a scoop of ice cream 🍨 One thing many tourists don’t know: Freddo espresso and freddo cappuccino are usually made with TWO shots of espresso. If you’d rather have a lighter coffee, ask for: ☕ Μονή Δόση (Moní Dósi) = single shot ☕ Ελαφρύ (Elafrý) = light My personal order? ☕ Ένα Φρέντο Καπουτσίνο Μέτριο, με Μαύρη Ζάχαρη, Κανέλα και Μονή Δόση (Ena Frénto Kapoutsíno Métrio, me Mávri Záchari, Kanéla kai Moní Dósi) A freddo cappuccino, medium sweet, with brown sugar, cinnamon and a single shot. Some more examples: ☕ Ένα Φραπέ Γλυκό με Γάλα (Ena Frappé Glykó me Gála) A sweet frappé with milk. ☕ Έναν Φρέντο Εσπρέσο Σκέτο (Enan Frénto Esprésso Skéto) A freddo espresso without sugar. ☕ Έναν Ελληνικό Καφέ Μέτριο (Enan Ellinikó Kafé Métrio) A medium-sweet Greek coffee. ☕ Ένα Φρέντο Καπουτσίνο με Γάλα Βρώμης και Στέβια (Ena Frénto Kapoutsíno me Gála Vrómis kai Stévia) A freddo cappuccino with oat milk and stevia. Now tell me YOUR perfect coffee order in the comments ☕👇 Write it in English and I’ll translate it into Greek for you. And if you want more practical Greece travel tips, Greek phrases, hidden gems and local knowledge, download my Ultimate Tourist Guide to Greece. It’s packed with the kind of information most tourists only learn after visiting Greece several times. #greecetravel #greekcoffee #greecetips #greecetiktok

Dumbbell Sumo Squat  Know the difference  1. Dumbbell Position Hold the dumbbell with both hands naturally hanging between your legs, rather than holding it at your chest. This allows you to lift heavier weights without being limited by arm strength. 2. Torso Posture Maintain a slight forward lean instead of staying fully upright. Leaning forward increases hip flexion, helping to stretch and better activate the glutes. 3. Stance Width and Foot Angle Set your feet about 1.5 times shoulder-width apart, with your toes pointing outward at roughly a 45-degree angle. If the stance is too wide, the inner thigh muscles (adductors) will take over, reducing glute activation. 4. Load Path As you squat down, the dumbbell should not stay directly under your shoulders. Instead, it should fall slightly behind the midline, closer to your posterior chain. Bring your hands slightly inward to keep the load closer to your center of mass, which helps reduce lower back strain and improves movement efficiency. #gymtips #quads #gluteworkout #gym #gymrat
